questions.text: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP, the energy currency of the cell, through oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.text: The site of photosynthesis in plant cells is the?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the organelles where photosynthesis takes place.

questions.text: According to the cell theory, all organisms are composed of one or more?
questions.explanation: The cell theory states that all organisms are made of cells.

questions.text: The cell theory states that new cells arise only by?
options: Division of a previously existing cell
questions.explanation: Cells arise only by division of a previously existing cell.

questions.text: The basic structural and functional unit of a living organism is the?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

questions.text: Which of the following is the genetic material of the cell?
questions.explanation: DNA is the genetic material that carries hereditary information.

questions.text: Which cell component synthesizes proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.text: The jelly-like fluid inside the cell in which organelles are found is the?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm consists of the jelly-like cytosol plus the cellular components.

questions.text: Which four components are common to ALL cells?
options: Cell wall, nucleus, DNA and ribosomes
Plasma membrane, cytoplasm, DNA and ribosomes
questions.explanation: All cells share a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, DNA and ribosomes.

questions.text: The outer covering that separates a cell's interior from its surrounding environment is the?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is the outer covering that separates the cell interior from its environment.

questions.text: Prokaryotic cells lack a true?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus; their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.

questions.text: The bacterial cell wall is made of which glycoprotein complex?
questions.explanation: The bacterial cell wall is made of murein, also called peptidoglycan.

questions.text: Which bacterial structure is very useful for genetic engineering?
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules used in genetic engineering.

questions.text: Hair-like protein appendages that help bacterial cells adhere to surfaces are called?
questions.explanation: Pili are hair-like proteinaceous appendages that help bacteria stick to surfaces and to each other.

questions.text: The thick polysaccharide layer found outside the bacterial cell wall is the?
questions.explanation: The capsule is a thick polysaccharide layer outside the cell wall of bacteria.

questions.text: A mass of sticky bacterial cells formed when many capsules fuse together is a?
questions.explanation: When capsules of many cells fuse together they form a sticky mass called a biofilm.

questions.text: The flagellum of a prokaryotic cell moves the cell forward by?
questions.explanation: The bacterial flagellum rotates in a corkscrew motion that drives the cell forward.

questions.text: Mesosomes are formed by infoldings of the?
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are folded invaginations of the prokaryotic plasma membrane.

questions.text: The photosynthetic pigments found in phototrophic bacteria are called?
questions.explanation: Bacteriochlorophylls are the photosynthetic pigments of phototrophic bacteria.

questions.text: The ribosomes of prokaryotic cells are of which type?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are the smaller 70S type made of 50S and 30S subunits.

questions.text: The genetic material of a prokaryotic cell consists of?
options: Circular double-stranded DNA not associated with proteins
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic genetic material is circular double-stranded DNA lying free in the cytoplasm.

questions.text: Prokaryotes appeared on Earth approximately how many years ago?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes appeared about 3500 million years ago.

questions.text: The hallmark of eukaryotic cells is?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells are characterized by compartmentalization into membrane-bounded organelles.

questions.text: Protista, fungi, plants and animals are all made up of?
questions.explanation: Protists, fungi, plants and animals are all composed of eukaryotic cells.

questions.text: The control center of the eukaryotic cell is the?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the control center that regulates the activities of the cell.

questions.text: The nucleolus is the site of synthesis of?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus synthesizes ribosomal RNA and ribosomal subunits.

questions.text: Which structure encloses and separates the contents of the nucleus from the rest of the cell?
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope (nuclear membrane) encloses the contents of the nucleus.

questions.text: Nuclear pores in the nuclear membrane enable substances to?
options: Pass into and out of the nucleus
questions.explanation: Nuclear pores allow substances such as nutrients and waste to move in and out of the nucleus.

questions.text: Which organelle is studded with ribosomes and is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: The rough ER carries ribosomes on its surface and is the site of protein synthesis.

questions.text: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is rough because of the presence of?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes attached to its surface make the rough ER appear rough.

questions.text: Lipid synthesis and drug detoxification occur in the?
questions.explanation: The smooth ER is the site of lipid synthesis, glycogenolysis and drug detoxification.

questions.text: The endoplasmic reticulum is connected to which membrane structure?
questions.explanation: The ER membrane is connected with the nuclear envelope.

questions.text: Which organelle packages and sorts proteins for secretion?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus packages, processes and sorts secretory materials.

questions.text: Lysosomes are organelles that contain?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain numerous hydrolytic enzymes that digest materials.

questions.text: Lysosomes originate from the?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes originate from the Golgi bodies.

questions.text: Which organelle is bounded by a double membrane, the inner one folded into cristae?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria have double membranes; the inner membrane is folded into cristae.

questions.text: ATP is produced mainly in which organelle?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria synthesize ATP by oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.text: The mitochondrial matrix contains?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix contains lipids, proteins, circular mtDNA and 55S ribosomes.

questions.text: Which organelles are described as semi-autonomous because they can synthesize some of their own proteins?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous because they synthesize some of their own proteins.

questions.text: The membrane enclosing each vacuole is called the?
questions.explanation: The vacuolar membrane is called the tonoplast.

questions.text: Which cell structure maintains turgor pressure inside plant cells?
questions.explanation: The vacuole maintains turgor pressure which keeps plant cells rigid.

questions.text: Anthocyanins, the pigments responsible for red, blue and purple colors of flowers, are found in?
questions.explanation: Anthocyanin pigments are sometimes present in cell vacuoles.

questions.text: Cell sap, found inside vacuoles, is a solution of?
questions.explanation: Cell sap is a solution of salts, sugars and organic acids.

questions.text: Tiny strands of cytoplasm that pass through pores in plant cell walls, connecting adjacent cells, are called?
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic strands that pass through pores connecting adjacent plant cells.

questions.text: The plant cell wall is made of?
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose.

questions.text: The fungal cell wall is made of?
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls contain chitin.

questions.text: A plant cell can be divided into two main parts, which are?
questions.explanation: The plant cell is divided into the cell wall and the protoplast.

questions.text: The plasma membrane is a?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is a flexible phospholipid bilayer.

questions.text: The plasma membrane is described as differentially permeable because it?
options: Controls the movement of solutes in and out of the cell
questions.explanation: A differentially permeable membrane controls the movement of solutes in and out of the cell.

questions.text: Microtubules are made up of which protein?
questions.explanation: Microtubules are made of the protein tubulin.

questions.text: Microtubules and microfilaments are part of the?
questions.explanation: Microtubules and microfilaments are components of the cytoskeleton.

questions.text: Clusters of ribosomes are known as?
questions.explanation: Clusters of ribosomes are called polyribosomes or polysomes.

questions.text: The main functional unit of the chloroplast is the?
questions.explanation: The grana are the main functional units of the chloroplast.

questions.text: The grana of a chloroplast are bathed in a homogeneous matrix called the?
questions.explanation: The grana are bathed in the stroma, which contains photosynthetic enzymes.

questions.text: Chloroplasts are a type of?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are pigmented plastids.

questions.text: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain which pigment?
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts contain carotene pigment, giving yellow, orange or red colors.

questions.text: Amyloplasts are non-pigmented plastids that store?
questions.explanation: Amyloplasts are leucoplasts that store starch.

questions.text: All plastids are derived from which small bodies?
questions.explanation: All types of plastids are derived from proplastids.

questions.text: If the development of a proplastid into a chloroplast is interrupted by lack of light, which structure is formed?
questions.explanation: An etioplast is formed when chloroplast development is interrupted by lack of light.

questions.text: Ergastic substances in cells are?
options: Products of metabolic activities, such as stored food and wastes
questions.explanation: Ergastic substances are products of metabolic activities, including stored food and wastes.

questions.text: Which stored food material is synthesized by the chloroplast?
questions.explanation: Starch is synthesized by the chloroplast.

questions.text: A group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function is a?
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function.

questions.text: The correct order of biological organization from simplest to most complex is?
options: Organ to tissue to cell to system
Cell to tissue to organ to organ system
Tissue to cell to organ to system
Organism to system to organ to tissue
questions.explanation: Levels of organization run from cell to tissue to organ to organ system.

questions.text: Spirogyra is an example of a form of cell organization known as?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a filament, formed by identical cells joined end to end.

questions.text: Volvox is an example of a?
questions.explanation: Volvox is a colony of similar cells joined together.

questions.text: Which organelle has F1 particles on its inner membrane for ATP synthesis?
questions.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane contains F1 particles for ATP synthesis.

questions.text: Mitosis produces how many daughter cells from one parent cell?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells from a single parent cell.

questions.text: The daughter cells produced by mitosis are?
options: Genetically identical to the parent cell
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces daughter cells identical to one another and to the parent cell.

questions.text: During which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align at the equatorial plate?
questions.explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes align at the equatorial plate.

questions.text: Sister chromatids separate and move toward the poles during which stage of mitosis?
questions.explanation: In anaphase, the centromeres divide and sister chromatids move to opposite poles.

questions.text: Gregor Mendel carried out his breeding experiments using which plant?
questions.explanation: Mendel used the common garden pea plant, Pisum sativum, for his heredity experiments.

questions.text: Mendel's findings on heredity were published in which year?
questions.explanation: Mendel's ideas were published in 1866.

questions.text: In Mendel's crosses of yellow-seeded and green-seeded peas, the F1 generation always had?
questions.explanation: The F1 generation always produced yellow seeds because yellow is dominant.

questions.text: Mendel's F2 generation in a monohybrid cross shows which typical phenotypic ratio?
questions.explanation: The F2 generation consistently shows a 3:1 ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes.

questions.text: The inherited "units" or "factors" described by Mendel are now called?
questions.explanation: Mendel's units of inheritance are now known as genes.

questions.text: Mendel's first law, stating that the two factors for each trait segregate during gamete formation, is also called the law of?
questions.explanation: Mendel's first law is the law of segregation, also known as the law of purity of gametes.

questions.text: Mendel's second law, which states that each inherited pair of factors separates independently of others, is the law of?
questions.explanation: Mendel's second law is the law of independent assortment.

questions.text: How many alleles for each trait does an individual inherit from each parent?
questions.explanation: An individual inherits one allele for each trait from each parent.

questions.text: An organism that has two identical alleles for a trait is described as?
questions.explanation: Having two identical alleles for a trait makes an organism homozygous.

questions.text: An organism that has two different alleles for a trait is described as?
questions.explanation: Having two different alleles for a trait makes an organism heterozygous.

questions.text: The observable physical characteristics of an organism are its?
questions.explanation: The phenotype is the observable physical characteristics of an organism.

questions.text: The genetic makeup of an organism is its?
questions.explanation: The genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism.

questions.text: The Punnett square technique was invented by which English geneticist?
questions.explanation: Reginald Punnett invented the Punnett square for predicting genotype combinations.

questions.text: In a cross between YY and GG pea plants, what percentage of the offspring will be heterozygous (YG)?
questions.explanation: YY x GG gives 100% heterozygous YG offspring.

questions.text: If yellow (Y) is dominant over green (G), what percentage of the offspring of a YG x YG cross will have the yellow phenotype?
questions.explanation: A YG x YG cross gives 75% yellow and 25% green phenotypes.

questions.text: In a YG x YG cross, what is the probability of a GG (homozygous recessive) offspring?
questions.explanation: Each box of a Punnett square represents a 25% chance, so GG offspring occur with 25% probability.

questions.text: An allele that masks the effect of another allele in the heterozygous condition is the?
questions.explanation: The dominant allele masks the expression of the recessive allele.

questions.text: A trait that is only expressed when two copies of its allele are present is called?
questions.explanation: A recessive trait is expressed only in the homozygous condition.

questions.text: Human body cells contain how many pairs of chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Human cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes.

questions.text: Of the 23 pairs of human chromosomes, how many pairs are autosomes?
questions.explanation: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.text: In mammals, which chromosome combination produces a male?
questions.explanation: In mammals, XY individuals are male.

questions.text: In mammals, which chromosome combination produces a female?
questions.explanation: In mammals, XX individuals are female.

questions.text: In birds, which chromosome combination produces a female?
questions.explanation: In birds, the female is the heterogametic sex, ZW.

questions.text: Cystic fibrosis, albinism and beta-thalassemia are examples of disorders caused by?
questions.explanation: These are recessive disorders that require two copies of the defective allele.

questions.text: Huntington disease is an example of a disorder caused by?
questions.explanation: Huntington disease is caused by a dominant allele; inheriting one copy causes the disorder.

questions.text: If both parents are carriers (Aa) of a recessive disease, what is the chance that a child is affected (aa)?
questions.explanation: An Aa x Aa cross gives a 25% chance of an aa (affected) child.

questions.text: If a carrier (Aa) mates with an affected individual (aa), what is the chance that their child is a healthy carrier?
questions.explanation: An Aa x aa cross gives a 50% chance of a carrier (Aa) child.

questions.text: Red and white four-o'clocks producing pink offspring is an example of?
questions.explanation: The pink intermediate phenotype results from incomplete dominance.

questions.text: In codominance, both alleles are?
questions.explanation: In codominance, both alleles are fully expressed in heterozygotes, as in AB blood type.

questions.text: The ABO blood group system is controlled by how many alleles?
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group is a multiple-allele series of three alleles: A, B and O.

questions.text: Traits determined by the combined effect of more than one pair of genes, such as human height, are called?
questions.explanation: Human height is a polygenic trait influenced by many genes.

questions.text: A single gene producing a variety of effects, as in sickle-cell anemia, is known as?
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene is responsible for a variety of traits.

questions.text: The subunits that make up a DNA molecule are called?
questions.explanation: DNA is a chain of subunits called nucleotides.

questions.text: The four nitrogenous bases found in DNA are?
questions.explanation: DNA contains the bases adenine, cytosine, guanine and thymine.

questions.text: Which sugar is found in DNA?
questions.explanation: DNA contains the sugar deoxyribose.

questions.text: Evolution is best defined as change over time in inherited traits of?
questions.explanation: Evolution is the change over time in inherited traits found in populations of organisms.

questions.text: The four common mechanisms of evolution are?
options: Natural selection, genetic drift, mutation and gene flow
Mutation, crossing over, fertilization and cloning
questions.explanation: Natural selection, genetic drift, mutation and gene flow are the four common mechanisms of evolution.

questions.text: The theory of natural selection was independently proposed by Darwin and Wallace in which year?
questions.explanation: Darwin and Wallace co-proposed the theory of natural selection in 1858.

questions.text: Darwin's famous book, On the Origin of Species, was published in which year?
questions.explanation: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.

questions.text: A mutation is best described as?
options: A permanent change in a DNA sequence
questions.explanation: Mutation is a permanent change in a DNA sequence.

questions.text: The word ecology comes from the Greek word "oikos", which means?
questions.explanation: Oikos means household or home, from which the word ecology is derived.

questions.text: The term "ecology" was coined in 1866 by which German scientist?
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel coined the word ecology in 1866.

questions.text: Ecology is the scientific study of?
options: The relation of living organisms to each other and their surroundings
questions.explanation: Ecology studies the relationships of living organisms to each other and their environment.

questions.text: The study of a particular single species and its relationship to its environment is called?
questions.explanation: Autecology is the study of a particular species and its ecology.

questions.text: The study of more than one species, that is, a community, is called?
questions.explanation: Synecology deals with the study of communities of more than one species.

questions.text: Which branch of ecology deals with translating ecological concepts into mathematical models used for prediction?
questions.explanation: Systems ecology translates ecological concepts into mathematical models for prediction.

questions.text: The branch of ecology that describes how organisms respond and adjust physiologically to the physical factors of the environment is?
questions.explanation: Physiological ecology deals with physiological responses of organisms to physical environmental factors.

questions.text: The zone of life on Earth, or the global sum of all ecosystems, is called the?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems, the zone of life on Earth.

questions.text: The largest ecosystem on Earth is the?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the largest ecosystem on Earth.

questions.text: The outer shell of the Earth's crust that supports life and provides materials for organisms is the?
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the outer shell of the Earth's crust which supports life.

questions.text: The body of liquid water on or near the surface of the Earth is called the?
questions.explanation: The hydrosphere is the body of liquid on or near the Earth's surface.

questions.text: Water covers approximately what percentage of the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Water covers about 71% of the Earth's surface.

questions.text: The role and position (the "job") of a species in nature is its?
questions.explanation: The niche is the functional role and position of a species in its ecosystem.

questions.text: The place where a plant or animal normally lives is its?
questions.explanation: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal normally lives.

questions.text: A group of organisms of the same species inhabiting a specific geographical locality at a particular time is a?
questions.explanation: A population is a group of organisms of the same species in a locality at a particular time.

questions.text: An assemblage of different species that interact with one another in a common area is a?
questions.explanation: A community is an assemblage of species interacting in a common area.

questions.text: The number of species in a community is called?
questions.explanation: Species richness is the number of species in a community.

questions.text: The relative abundance of the different species in a community is called?
questions.explanation: Species evenness is the measure of the relative abundance of different species.

questions.text: The Shannon-Wiener index is a commonly applied measure of?
questions.explanation: The Shannon-Wiener index is used to measure species diversity.

questions.text: Green plants that convert CO2, water and solar energy into food by photosynthesis are described as?
questions.explanation: Green plants are primary producers that fix and store energy by photosynthesis.

questions.text: Organisms that break down dead organic matter into mineral components used by plants are?
questions.explanation: Decomposers, mainly fungi and bacteria, break down dead organic matter.

questions.text: A linear feeding relationship that shows what eats what is called a?
questions.explanation: A food chain is a linear feeding relationship showing what eats what.

questions.text: A complex network of feeding relationships in a community is called a?
questions.explanation: A food web is a complex feeding relationship of species in a community.

questions.text: Which organisms occupy the first trophic level of a food chain?
questions.explanation: Producers (green plants) always occupy the first trophic level.

questions.text: As energy moves from one trophic level to the next, each higher level typically contains what percentage of the energy of the level below it?
questions.explanation: Each succeeding trophic level contains less than 10% of the energy of the level below.

questions.text: For animal consumers, energy for maintenance usually constitutes what proportion of the assimilated energy?
questions.explanation: Energy for maintenance 'R' usually makes up more than 90% of the assimilated energy in animal consumers.

questions.text: The collection of stamens forming the male reproductive organs of a flower is called the?
questions.explanation: The androecium is the collection of stamens, the male organs of the flower.

questions.text: The collection of carpels forming the female reproductive organs of a flower is the?
questions.explanation: The gynoecium is the collection of carpels, the female organs of the flower.

questions.text: A stamen is made up of which two parts?
questions.explanation: A stamen consists of an anther and a filament.

questions.text: Pollen grains are produced in which part of the stamen?
questions.explanation: The anther contains the pollen sacs in which pollen is made.

questions.text: Which part of the carpel receives pollen grains during pollination?
questions.explanation: The stigma is the part of the carpel that receives pollen grains.

questions.text: The stalk that bears the stigma in a suitable position in the flower is the?
questions.explanation: The style bears the stigma in a suitable position to receive pollen.

questions.text: The swollen hollow base of the carpel that contains one or more ovules is the?
questions.explanation: The ovary is the swollen base of the carpel containing the ovules.

questions.text: After fertilization, the ovule develops into the?
questions.explanation: Following fertilization, the ovule becomes the seed.

questions.text: After fertilization, the ovary of a flower develops into the?
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovary develops into the fruit.

questions.text: The collection of sepals is called the?
questions.explanation: The calyx is the collection of sepals.

questions.text: The collection of petals of a flower is called the?
questions.explanation: The corolla is the collection of petals.

questions.text: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma is called?
questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.

questions.text: Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to?
options: A stigma of another plant only
A stigma of the same flower or a flower of the same plant
questions.explanation: Self-pollination transfers pollen to the stigma of the same flower or the same plant.

questions.text: Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anthers of?
options: One plant to the stigma of another plant
One flower to its own stigma
One anther to the other anther
questions.explanation: Cross-pollination transfers pollen from one plant to the stigma of another plant.

questions.text: The fusion of the male and female gametes is called?
questions.explanation: Fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes.

questions.text: In flowering plants, the second male nucleus fuses with the diploid nucleus to form the?
questions.explanation: The second male nucleus fuses with the diploid nucleus to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.text: Double fertilization, which occurs only in flowering plants, leads to the formation of which two structures in the seed?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization produces the embryo and the endosperm.

questions.text: A collection of flowers borne on the same stalk is an?
questions.explanation: An inflorescence is a collection of flowers borne on the same stalk.

questions.text: The topmost part of the flower stalk from which the other parts of the flower arise is the?
questions.explanation: The receptacle is the topmost part of the flower stalk from which flower parts arise.

questions.text: A flower that has both male and female reproductive organs is described as?
questions.explanation: Hermaphrodite or bisexual plants have both male and female sex organs.

questions.text: Plants in which the male and female sex organs are borne on separate plants, such as yew and willow, are called?
questions.explanation: Dioecious plants bear male and female organs on separate plants.

questions.text: Plants that bear separate male and female flowers on the same plant, such as oak and hazel, are called?
questions.explanation: Monoecious plants bear separate male and female flowers on the same plant.

questions.text: Which artificial propagation method transfers a scion onto the lower part of another plant (the stock)?
questions.explanation: Grafting is the transfer of one plant (scion) onto the lower part of another plant (stock).

questions.text: The cloning or propagation of plants by tissue culture is called?
questions.explanation: Micropropagation is the cloning of plants by tissue culture.

questions.text: New plants produced from bulbs, corms, rhizomes and tubers are a result of?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation produces new plants from vegetative parts such as bulbs, corms and rhizomes.

questions.text: Genetically identical offspring produced from a single parent are referred to as?
questions.explanation: Identical offspring from a single parent are referred to as clones.

questions.text: In budding, the new plant develops from an outgrowth on the parent body called a?
questions.explanation: Budding occurs when a new plant develops from an outgrowth called a bud.

questions.text: In the lupin flower, the uppermost petal is called the?
questions.explanation: The uppermost petal of the lupin flower is the standard.

questions.text: In the lupin flower, the two partly joined petals forming a boat-shaped structure are the?
questions.explanation: The two partly joined side petals of the lupin are the wings.

questions.text: The ovary located above the other flower parts, as in a hypogynous flower, is described as?
questions.explanation: A superior ovary is located above the other flower parts as in a hypogynous flower.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of all living organisms?
questions.explanation: Movement is one of the features shared by all living organisms.

questions.text: The four major categories of biological macromolecules are?
options: Nucleic acids, proteins, carbohydrates and lipids
Sugars, amino acids, fatty acids and bases
questions.explanation: The four major biological macromolecules are nucleic acids, proteins, carbohydrates and lipids.

questions.text: The essential chemical processes by which organisms acquire nutrients and obtain energy are together called?
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the set of essential chemical processes in living organisms.

questions.text: Metabolism is often viewed as the interaction of which two types of reactions?
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the interaction of breaking (catabolic) and building (anabolic) reactions.

questions.text: The study of complex metabolic functions is called?
questions.explanation: The study of complex metabolic functions is physiology.

questions.text: The transformation that occurs from one developmental stage to another, such as from larva to adult, is called?
questions.explanation: The transformation from one stage to another is called metamorphosis.

questions.text: The property of organisms to respond to environmental stimuli is called?
questions.explanation: All organisms respond to environmental stimuli, a property called irritability.

questions.text: The faithful transmission of traits from parents to offspring is called?
questions.explanation: Heredity is the faithful transmission of traits from parents to offspring.

questions.text: The production of differences among the traits of different individuals is called?
questions.explanation: Variation is the production of differences among the traits of different individuals.

questions.text: The process by which one species splits into two or more different species is called?
questions.explanation: Speciation is the process by which a species splits into new species.

questions.text: Who is regarded as the Father of Biological Classification?
questions.explanation: Aristotle is considered the Father of Biological Classification.

questions.text: Carolus Linnaeus is known as the father of?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus is called the Father of Taxonomy.

questions.text: Linnaeus published his famous book, Systema Naturae, in which year?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus published Systema Naturae in 1758.

questions.text: The system of naming organisms using two Latinized names (genus and species) is called?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature: a two-word Latinized name for each species.

questions.text: In binomial nomenclature, the first word of the name indicates the?
questions.explanation: The first word of a binomial name gives the genus.

questions.text: In binomial nomenclature, the second word of the name indicates the?
questions.explanation: The second word of a binomial name gives the species.

questions.text: John Ray provided the first good definition of a species as?
questions.explanation: John Ray defined the species as a reproducing unit.

questions.text: Which scientist's work marked the beginning of the use of phylogeny in systematics?
questions.explanation: Lamarck arranged animals according to evolution, beginning the use of phylogeny in systematics.

questions.text: Which scientist insisted that extinct fossil forms should be included in the table of classification?
questions.explanation: Cuvier insisted that extinct fossil forms be included in classification.

questions.text: The largest phylum in the animal kingdom is?
questions.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest phylum, containing over 90% of known animal species.

questions.text: Which class of the phylum Arthropoda is the most successful and diverse group of animals?
questions.explanation: Insects (Insecta) number about 750,000 species, making them the most diverse animal group.

questions.text: Members of which phylum are known as sponges?
questions.explanation: Sponges belong to the phylum Porifera.

questions.text: Which phylum is distinguished by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal tubular nerve cord and gill slits in the pharynx?
questions.explanation: Chordates are distinguished by a notochord, dorsal tubular nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits.

questions.text: Fungi are organisms that?
questions.explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll and are therefore heterotrophic like animals.

questions.text: Fungi consist of fine tubular branching threads called?
questions.explanation: The body of a fungus consists of tubular threads called hyphae.

questions.text: Mosses and liverworts belong to which plant division?
questions.explanation: Mosses and liverworts are bryophytes.

questions.text: Which group of plants has no true roots and no vascular tissues, and is anchored by rhizoids?
questions.explanation: Mosses have no true roots or vascular tissues and are anchored by rhizoids.

questions.text: Ferns, which have true roots, feathery leaves, underground stems and vascular tissues, belong to which division?
questions.explanation: Ferns are pteridophytes, the earliest known vascular plants.

questions.text: Gymnosperms such as pines bear their seeds?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary.

questions.text: Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants whose seeds are?
questions.explanation: Angiosperm seeds are enclosed in an ovary, giving more protection.

questions.text: A close relationship between two organisms of different species in which both partners benefit is called?
questions.explanation: Symbiosis is a close relationship in which both partners benefit.

questions.text: A relationship in which one organism benefits while the other is neither benefited nor harmed is called?
questions.explanation: Commensalism is a positive-neutral relationship where one partner is unaffected.

questions.text: An organism that lives in or on another organism, called the host, and feeds at its expense is a?
questions.explanation: A parasite lives in or on the host and feeds at the host's expense.

questions.text: The relationship in which one organism hunts, kills and directly feeds on another organism (the prey) is called?
questions.explanation: Predation is the relationship in which a predator hunts, kills and feeds on its prey.
